newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK CAPITAL MKT COMMISSION WARNS AGAINST SPECULATION.
newsitem.headline: GREEK CAPITAL MKT COMMISSION WARNS AGAINST SPECULATION.

text.p: Greece's capital market commission said on Wednesday the stock market's rally was a healthy upside correction in terms of volume and valuations but warned investors to avoid rumour-based investment decisions.

"The rise in stock prices over the last two months was a healthy upside correction as shares had been undervalued for a long period," capital market commission president Stavros Thomadakis told reporters.
"The confidence of foreign investors is also a welcome development," he added.
But the stock market's continuous and sharp advances had the commission worried as this could give rise to speculative conditions fueled by rumours.
This prompted the commission's intervention on Thursday. It urged the investment public to exercise caution in its investment decisions.
"It is necessary to recommend to the retail investment public especially to avoid investment decisions based on rumours, to be cool-headed and careful in their choices," Thomadakis said.
Asked by reporters to explain the rationale for Thursday's presser, the commission's president underlined that its aim was not to reverse the market's uptrend.
However the rally's acceleration in the last few days prompted the commission's statement, he said.
"We do not believe or wish to point out that the stock market is overvalued," said Thomadakis noting that the critical element in terms of investor protection was "self-protection".
Stocks jumped 3.26 percent on Wednesday, continuing their bull run in very heavy volume of 44.8 billion drachmas. Advancers led decliners 162 to 71 with 25 issues unchanged.
The benchmark general share index settled at 1,453.60 points, up 45.95. Bank shares led the advance with the sector index gaining 4.90 percent. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
